title: What if a tsunami hit your cruise ship? You're on the pool deck, 300 miles from land. The alarm goes off, nobody moves. Then someone at the rail starts screaming: a wall of water is coming from the side, taller than a skyscraper, and the ship can't turn in time. Where would you run? 👇 #whatif #pov #simulation #science #fyp

analysis_notes.visual_change_detection: ffmpeg scene filter (threshold 0.12) finds a single hard cut at 62.1 s (deck -> underwater). Everything else is one continuous simulated camera with pans/turns; plus a fade to black ~70-72 s and an end card from ~73 s.
analysis_notes.platform_label: TikTok shows an 'AI-generated' label in the corner. Visuals look like a real-time low-poly 3D scene (game-engine / Three.js style) rather than diffusion video.
analysis_notes.control_note: Same channel, same format, same week as the 13.4M-view outlier 7693305573487562016 (oxygen). This one performed at channel median (0.97x). Likely differences: the premise is less surprising (a tsunami hitting a ship is an expected disaster, while the oxygen one has counter-intuitive science consequences), the first 30 s are a long, low-stakes setup with almost no visual change (walking past sun loungers), the payoff is a generic 'wave hits camera' with no clever twist, and the end card admits the premise is unrealistic (open-ocean tsunamis are ~3 ft), undercutting the sim.

title_pattern.template: What if a [disaster] hit your [everyday-luxury place]? + 'You're on the [specific spot], [N] miles from [safety].' + 2-3 escalating story sentences (alarm ignored -> someone screams -> threat bigger than [familiar tall thing] -> escape fails) + engagement CTA 'Where would you run? 👇' + #whatif #pov #simulation #science #fyp
title_pattern.notes: Identical caption formula to the channel's outlier (question + second-person placement + escalation + CTA question). The caption here adds narrative details not in the video (alarm, someone screaming) - the caption is a mini-story, not a description. Note the caption is more dramatic than the video itself.

thumbnail.source: TikTok originCover = first frame of the video (no designed thumbnail)
thumbnail.composition: 9:16 low-poly 3D render from eye height walking down a cruise pool deck: wooden plank walkway in the lower-left foreground converging toward a small teal-roofed deck bar in mid-right, rows of blue sun loungers on the right, blocky low-poly passengers in the middle, seagulls in a blue sky top half with a hazy horizon line at ~43% height. Diagonal palm-leaf shadows across the deck.
thumbnail.text: Centered white serif (Garamond/Cormorant-like) two-line title at ~25-30% height: 'What if a tsunami / hit your cruise ship?'. HUD at left ~47% height: tiny tracked sans caps 'OCEAN DEPTH', large thin serif numerals '16,716 ft', tiny caps 'BELOW THE HULL'.
thumbnail.colours: Bright daytime palette: sky blue gradient to pale cream at the horizon, warm brown/tan wood deck, grey deck plates, navy loungers, teal accents; white text only. Sunny and calm - nothing in frame signals danger.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Weak: no single subject, no visible threat; the only scale cue is the HUD number (16,716 ft of water under you) contrasting with a tiny deck. The wave never appears in the cover.
thumbnail.why_it_works: The calm vacation 'before' plus a big depth number and the word 'tsunami' lets the viewer imagine the disaster; the premium serif/HUD look signals a polished simulation. Weakness compared with the channel's outlier: the cover is a generic deck with no tension object (no countdown clock, no wave sliver on the horizon), so it relies entirely on the title.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: (on-screen, no voice) 'What if a tsunami hit your cruise ship?' over a sunny pool deck, slow forward walk; HUD 'OCEAN DEPTH 16,716 ft BELOW THE HULL' with the number jittering live.
hook.verbatim_0_15s: What if a tsunami hit your cruise ship? / You are on deck, 300 miles from land. / The ocean below you is three miles deep.
hook.device: Question title + second-person POV placement + live HUD metric (ocean depth) that jitters to feel 'live'. Unlike the outlier, there is no countdown or ticking clock in the hook and no event in the first 15 s - the threat (TSUNAMI 115 mi, 500 mph counter) only arrives at ~17 s. Setup facts (300 miles from land, three miles deep) build isolation/vulnerability but give no immediate payoff.

beats.summary: Title question over a calm sunny cruise pool deck; slow first-person walk past loungers; HUD OCEAN DEPTH ~16,716 ft BELOW THE HULL; seagulls overhead.
'You are on deck, 300 miles from land.' Camera keeps strolling among passengers and loungers - isolation established.
'The ocean below you is three miles deep.' Camera turns left to reveal the pool and waterslide tower; depth counter still on screen.
HUD flips to 'TSUNAMI 115.2 mi / 500 MILES AN HOUR' and starts counting down fast. 'Far away, the seafloor jumps.' Music level steps up. Nothing visible changes on deck (dramatic irony).
'The tsunami moves as fast as a jet.' Distance drops from ~50 to ~8 mi while camera drifts back over loungers; passengers oblivious.
Camera turns to the rail and the open sea. 'Out here, it is barely three feet tall.' Distance 4.6 -> 3.0 mi - the real-science fact that ships don't notice tsunamis.
HUD flips to 'WAVE HEIGHT 102 ft / x.x MILES AWAY' and rises fast; a teal band appears on the horizon. 'Not this one.' Passengers at the rail start reacting.
Camera swings across the deck: 'It is coming from the side.' People run; camera briefly looks aft at the white superstructure with a passenger waving arms (~45-47 s). Wave 500 -> 830 ft.
Camera returns to the rail: a huge teal wall fills the upper frame, sky darkens. 'The ship cannot turn in time.' Wave 865 -> 1,040 ft, 1.4 -> 0.7 miles away.
'It is taller than a skyscraper.' Wave curls overhead, 1,070 -> 1,190 ft; distance switches from miles to feet (520 FEET AWAY -> 175).
'There is nowhere left to run.' Spray and foam break over the deck, loungers tumble at camera, counter reaches 1,300 ft / 0 FEET AWAY; audio peaks.
Hard cut underwater: HUD 'THE WAVE / HERE'. Bubbles, floating life rings, umbrellas and silhouetted bodies drift; cracked-glass lens overlays spread; scene darkens to black.

Near-black card repeats the title question, then tiny mono caps: 'In the open ocean, tsunamis rarely top 3 feet - ships at sea usually don't notice them pass.' Audio near silent. Loops back to the title frame.

pacing.note_wpm: No narration. 10 italic serif caption lines (3-8 words) plus the title; each held ~3-5 s with 2-4 s caption-free gaps; new line roughly every 5-6 s. 54 wpm over the 80 s on reading pace (72 wpm counting the end card).
pacing.note_shots: Only one hard cut (62.1 s) plus a fade to black and the end card - effectively a single-take simulated camera. Counting camera re-framings as shots gives ~16 segments (avg ~5 s), noticeably slower than the outlier (~2.4 s). 0-34 s is nearly static touring of the deck; real visual escalation only begins at 34 s (wave appears) - 43% of runtime before the threat is visible.
pacing.hud_cadence: HUD label changes 3 times (OCEAN DEPTH 0-17 s -> TSUNAMI distance/speed 17-35 s -> WAVE HEIGHT + distance 35-62 s -> THE WAVE HERE 62-70 s). The number ticks every frame, giving constant motion even when the scene is calm.
pacing.time_scale: Tsunami covers ~112 mi in ~18 s on screen (compressed time, ~1,000x faster than 500 mph), then the wave grows 102 -> 1,300 ft in ~27 s. Inverse of the outlier's slow-motion trick.
pacing.caption_style: Centered white italic serif, ~30 px at 576 wide, at ~70% frame height, fade in/out, no box. Title: upright serif, larger, at ~27% height. HUD at left ~47% height: tiny tracked sans caps label, big thin serif number with unit, tiny caps sub-line.
pacing.audio_curve: Bed -24 dB -> -18 dB when the tsunami is announced -> crescendo to -8 dB at impact -> silence on the end card.

techniques_worth_copying: Three-stage HUD that re-labels itself with the story (OCEAN DEPTH -> TSUNAMI distance at 500 MPH -> WAVE HEIGHT + FEET AWAY -> 'THE WAVE / HERE'); unit switch from miles to feet at the last moment makes proximity feel sudden.
Dramatic irony: the HUD shows the threat approaching while passengers on screen stay oblivious.
Real-science false reassurance then twist: 'Out here, it is barely three feet tall.' / 'Not this one.' - a 3-word re-hook at the midpoint.
Caption ladder of short declaratives that each raise stakes along a different axis: location -> depth -> cause -> speed -> (false calm) -> direction -> helplessness -> scale comparison -> no escape.
Familiar scale comparison ('taller than a skyscraper') timed with the camera tilting up at the wall of water.
Impact -> hard cut underwater -> cracked-lens overlays -> fade to black: a clean 'you didn't make it' ending without gore.
End card that repeats the title question plus a tiny real-fact disclaimer (credibility, comment bait, loop back to the start).
Audio as escalation: bed volume steps up at the inciting event and crescendos to the impact, then cuts to silence.
what_to_avoid_vs_outlier: Don't spend 30+ s on calm setup with no visible change; put a countdown or visible threat on screen in the first 3 s (the outlier's live countdown hits zero at 8 s).
Avoid an obvious premise whose outcome the viewer can predict; the outlier wins with counter-intuitive consequences (river becomes hydrogen, concrete crumbles).
A fact-check end card that says the premise wouldn't happen can deflate shares; if used, frame it as a surprising fact rather than a debunk.
Cover frame has no tension object; add the threat (wave sliver on the horizon, ticking clock) to frame 0.

code_only_remake_needs.summary: Feasible in Remotion with a fake-3D (2.5D) approach or react-three-fiber; the look is flat-shaded low-poly, no textures, so it suits code.
code_only_remake_needs.scene: Low-poly cruise deck: plank walkway, grey deck plates, rows of navy/yellow loungers (instanced boxes), deck bar with teal roof, umbrellas (cone + pole), railing, pool (flat turquoise plane), waterslide tower, white superstructure block. Gradient sky, hazy horizon, flat ocean plane, a few seagull V-sprites. Blocky stick passengers (box limbs) with 2-3 simple loop animations (walk, stand, run, wave arms). Palm-leaf shadow overlay as a soft dark SVG texture.
code_only_remake_needs.camera: Scripted single camera path with keyframed position/yaw/pitch: forward walk with head-bob, left pan to pool, right pan to rail, quick 180 turn, tilt up, then shake/roll on impact. In 2.5D: parallax layers per depth band and SVG/CSS transforms; in R3F: a spline camera.
code_only_remake_needs.wave: Teal wall: an extruded curved mesh or layered SVG path whose height animates from a 4 px horizon band to filling the frame, with a lighter crest, white foam streak strokes, diagonal spray lines, then full-frame white foam wipe on impact.
code_only_remake_needs.underwater: Full-frame teal gradient + dark vignette, particle bubbles (circles rising), drifting debris sprites (ring, umbrella, lounger, silhouettes) with slow rotation, light shafts, three SVG spider-crack overlays scaling in, fade to black.
code_only_remake_needs.hud_and_captions: HUD component: label (tracked caps sans) + big thin serif number interpolated per frame with toLocaleString and unit + sub-line; label/unit switches by beat; small random jitter for 'live' depth readout. Caption component: italic serif, centered at 70% height, 0.3 s fade in/out, one line per beat. Title and end card in upright serif with a mono caps fact line.
code_only_remake_needs.audio: Ambient sea/wind + music bed with volume automation keyed to beats, low rumble rising from 34 s, impact boom + underwater muffle filter at the cut, silence on the end card. No VO needed (optional Kokoro TTS if we add narration).
code_only_remake_needs.storyboard_fields: Per beat: t_start/t_end, caption, camera keyframe, hud {label, from, to, unit, sub}, wave_height_px, sky_tint, shake_amount, audio_gain.
